name: Attentional Selection
description: Biased competition among representations: attention enhances responses to attended stimuli and suppresses unattended ones. Implemented via gain modulation of sensory responses and top-down feedback from parietal and prefrontal cortex.
key_references: Desimone, R., & Duncan, J. (1995). Neural mechanisms of selective visual attention. Annual Review of Neuroscience, 18, 193-222.
Reynolds, J. H., & Chelazzi, L. (2004). Attentional modulation of visual processing. Annual Review of Neuroscience, 27, 611-647.
empirical_evidence: Single-unit recordings show enhanced responses to attended stimuli (Duncan, Desimone). Visual search tasks show attentional effects on RTs and errors. fMRI shows attention-dependent activity in V1 and beyond. Parietal cortex causal role shown via microstimulation (Wardak et al.). Mechanism via top-down feedback somewhat debated.
